items.claim: Replica-served GET miss now removes a live entry's index member
items.consequence: With redis_cluster2 configured for replica reads (routeByLatency=true, or useReadOnly=true), go-redis routes read-only commands (GET, EXISTS, ZRANGEBYLEX) to replicas while ZREM and ZADD go to the master. A listing that runs shortly after an InsertEntry can read the member from an up-to-date node but GET the value from a lagging replica, receive redis.Nil, and the new code then ZREMs the live entry's member on the master; the follow-up EXISTS is also replica-routed and confirms the stale miss, so no ZAddNX repair happens. The entry stays reachable by path but is permanently absent from listings, and DeleteFolderChildren, which iterates the index, will never delete it; UpdateEntry only SETs the value and never re-adds the member, so the hole persists until another InsertEntry at that exact path. Before this diff the same stale read cost one transiently skipped entry with no write; the diff turns an eventually-consistent read into a durable index mutation. Confirming the miss against the slot master, or disabling the repair when replica reads are enabled, removes the trigger.
items.proposed_fix: Make the orphan repair master-authoritative before it mutates the index. In removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember, confirm absence of the value key against the slot master before the ZRem and bail out when it exists: when store.Client is a *redis.ClusterClient, obtain the master with MasterForKey(ctx, store.getKey(string(path))) and run EXISTS on that client, and use the same master-routed client for the post-ZRem re-check; non-cluster clients already target the master. A simpler, more conservative alternative: record the useReadOnly/routeByLatency flags on UniversalRedis2Store in RedisCluster2Store.initialize and skip the repair (restoring the old skip-only behaviour) when either is set, documenting that index self-heal requires master reads.

Scenario: InsertEntry /d/f SETs the value on the master for slot(/d/f) and ZADD NX on the master for slot(/d\x00); replication to the value slot's replica lags. A concurrent listing of /d reads member f via ZRANGEBYLEX, GETs /d/f on the lagging replica and gets nil, so FindEntry returns ErrNotFound; line 208 calls the repair; line 238 ZREMs f on the index master; line 245 EXISTS is replica-routed and returns 0; the function returns without ZADD. Result: value present on master, index member gone, every later listing of /d omits f.
Pre-diff behaviour at the same point was `err = nil; continue` with no write (git diff db5a086d..6c8fde66), so this consequence is introduced by the diff.

native_payload.intent: Make redis2 directory listings self-heal the per-directory ZSET index by removing members whose value key no longer exists (Redis TTL expiry, out-of-band DEL, a DeleteEntry that failed between its DEL and ZREM), and keep the index member when a concurrent InsertEntry recreated the value between the FindEntry miss and the ZRem. Must not make live entries disappear from listings, must honor keyPrefix, and must not fail the listing when a repair fails.

residual_risks: Narrow window in which the post-ZRem ZAddNX (universal_redis_store.go:250) recreates the `<dir>\x00` index key after a concurrent DeleteFolderChildren + DeleteEntry(dir) has already deleted it: EXISTS must observe the child value before DeleteFolderChildren DELs it and the ZAddNX must land after DeleteEntry's DEL of the index key. Leaves a one-member index for a deleted directory; the same shape already exists for InsertEntry's ZAddNX at :68, so this is not new in kind, only a second trigger.

When the EXISTS re-check at universal_redis_store.go:245 fails with a transport error, exists is 0 with err != nil and the code falls through to ZAddNX, re-adding the member it just removed. This is the conservative direction (the member is retried on the next listing) but it means a flaky connection can make the repair a no-op indefinitely for that member; noted, not a defect.

Single-master interleavings of the repair with InsertEntry (SET then ZADD NX), DeleteEntry (DEL then ZREM) and UpdateEntry (SET only) were traced by both reads and no hole was found on a linearizable master; the finding above is the one ordering that breaks the author's 'member cannot outlive a missing value' invariant, and it needs replica-routed reads. The analysis assumes no writer of the `<dir>\x00` ZSET outside redis2 (grep over weed/ found only InsertEntry, DeleteEntry, DeleteFolderChildren, ListDirectoryEntries); external tooling writing the index directly is outside that boundary.

Pre-existing, not introduced here: weed/command/scaffold/filer.toml advertises `readOnly` for [redis_cluster2] while RedisCluster2Store.Initialize reads `useReadOnly`, so the scaffold key is a silent no-op; `routeByLatency` is wired correctly and alone suffices to trigger finding #1.

Pre-existing, not introduced here: members skipped via `continue` in ListDirectoryEntries are not counted toward the requested limit and are invisible to filer.doListDirectoryEntries's expiredCount re-list (weed/filer/filer.go:451-479), so a page over a dirty index can come back short and Filer.ListDirectoryEntries's hasMore (limit+1) can read false early. The diff reduces exposure, since orphans are gone after the first listing, but that first listing still under-fills.
testing_gaps: All three new tests skip unless RUN_REDIS_TESTS=1 and a live redis-server is present (verified: `go test -count=1 -v ./weed/filer/redis2/` passes with every test SKIP), so the default package run and CI exercise none of the new code; a green build does not verify the repair, the re-add branch, or keyPrefix handling.

TestRemoveOrphanedDirectoryListMemberKeepsRecreatedEntry calls the helper directly against a live value and only with an empty keyPrefix; it does not exercise the interleaving the second commit targets (InsertEntry's SET landing between FindEntry's miss and the ZRem with its ZADD NX a no-op) through ListDirectoryEntries, and the re-add path is never run with a keyPrefix set.

No test covers the cluster store with ReadOnly/RouteByLatency and a lagging replica (finding #1); an injected redis.UniversalClient wrapper that returns redis.Nil for GET/EXISTS while the write path holds the key would reproduce it without a real cluster.
